247 248 #### Keyboard Button Mini Apps 249 250 >**TL;DR:** Mini Apps launched from a **web_app** type [keyboard button](/bots/api/types/keyboardbutton.md) can send data back to the bot in a *service message* using [Telegram.WebApp.sendData](#initializing-mini-apps). This makes it possible for the bot to produce a response without communicating with any external servers. 251 252 Users can interact with bots using [custom keyboards](/bots.md#keyboards), [buttons under bot messages](/bots.md#inline-keyboards-and-on-the-fly-updating), as well as by sending freeform **text messages** or any of the **attachment types** supported by Telegram: photos and videos, files, locations, contacts and polls. For even more flexibility, bots can utilize the full power of **HTML5** to create user-friendly input interfaces. 253 254 You can send a **web_app** type [KeyboardButton](/bots/api/types/keyboardbutton.md) that opens a Mini App from the specified URL. 255 256 To transmit data from the user back to the bot, the Mini App can call the [Telegram.WebApp.sendData](#initializing-mini-apps) method. Data will be transmitted to the bot as a String in a service message. The bot can continue communicating with the user after receiving it. 257 258 **Good for:** 259 260 - **Сustom data input interfaces** (a personalized calendar for selecting dates; selecting data from a list with advanced search options; a randomizer that lets the user "spin a wheel" and chooses one of the available options, etc.) 261 - **Reusable components** that do not depend on a particular bot. 262 263 #### Inline Button Mini Apps 264 265 > **TL;DR:** For more interactive Mini Apps like [@DurgerKingBot](https://t.me/durgerkingbot), use a **web_app** type [Inline KeyboardButton](/bots/api/types/inlinekeyboardbutton.md), which gets basic user information and can be used to send a message on behalf of the user to the chat with the bot. 266 267 If receiving text data alone is insufficient or you need a more advanced and personalized interface, you can open a Mini App using a **web_app** type [Inline KeyboardButton](/bots/api/types/inlinekeyboardbutton.md). 268 269 From the button, a Mini App will open with the URL specified in the button. In addition to the user's [theme settings](#color-schemes), it will receive basic user information (`ID`, `name`, `username`, `language_code`) and a unique identifier for the session, **query_id**, which allows messages on behalf of the user to be sent back to the bot. 270 271 The bot can call the Bot API method [answerWebAppQuery](/bots/api/methods/answerwebappquery.md) to send an inline message from the user back to the bot and close the Mini App. After receiving the message, the bot can continue communicating with the user. 272 273 **Good for:** 274 275 - Fully-fledged web services and integrations of any kind. 276 - The use cases are effectively **unlimited**. 277 278 #### Launching Mini Apps from the Menu Button 279 280 >**TL;DR:** Mini Apps can be launched from a customized menu button. This simply offers a quicker way to access the app and is otherwise **identical** to [launching a mini app from an inline button](#inline-button-mini-apps). === 396-415 === 396 ### Initializing Mini Apps 397 398 To connect your Mini App to the Telegram client, place the script [telegram-web-app.js]({telegram_web_app_script_url}) in the `` tag before any other scripts, using this code: 399 400 ``` 401 402 ``` 403 404 Once the script is connected, a `window.Telegram.WebApp` object will become available with the following fields: 405 406 | Field | Type | Description | 407 |-----------| 408 | initData |String|A string with raw data transferred to the Mini App, convenient for [validating data](#validating-data-received-via-the-mini-app).\ 409 **WARNING:** [Validate data](#validating-data-received-via-the-mini-app) from this field before using it on the bot's server.| 410 | initDataUnsafe |[WebAppInitData](#webappinitdata)|An object with input data transferred to the Mini App.\ 411 **WARNING:** Data from this field should not be trusted. You should only use data from *initData* on the bot's server and only after it has been [validated](#validating-data-received-via-the-mini-app). | 412 | version |String|The version of the Bot API available in the user's Telegram app.| 413 | platform |String|The name of the platform of the user's Telegram app.| 414 | colorScheme |String|The color scheme currently used in the Telegram app. Either “light” or “dark”. \ 415 Also available as the CSS variable `var(--tg-color-scheme)`.| === 980,1000 === 980 #### WebAppInitData 981 982 This object contains data that is transferred to the Mini App when it is opened. It is empty if the Mini App was launched from a [keyboard button](#keyboard-button-mini-apps) or from [inline mode](#inline-mode-mini-apps). 983 984 | Field | Type | Description | 985 |--------------|-------------|-----------------| 986 | query_id | String | _Optional._ A unique identifier for the Mini App session, required for sending messages via the [answerWebAppQuery](/bots/api/methods/answerwebappquery.md) method. | 987 | chat_join_request_query_id | String | _Optional._ A unique identifier for the chat join request query, required for processing the query via the method [answerChatJoinRequestQuery](/bots/api/methods/answerchatjoinrequestquery.md). | 988 | user | [WebAppUser](#webappuser) | _Optional._ An object containing data about the current user. | 989 | receiver | [WebAppUser](#webappuser) | _Optional._ An object containing data about the chat partner of the current user in the chat where the bot was launched via the attachment menu. Returned only for private chats and only for Mini Apps launched via the attachment menu. | 990 | chat | [WebAppChat](#webappchat) | _Optional._ An object containing data about the chat where the bot was launched via the attachment menu or the chat to which the join request query was sent. Returned for supergroups, channels and group chats – only for Mini Apps launched via the attachment menu and chat join requests. | 991 | chat_type | String | _Optional._ Type of the chat from which the Mini App was opened. Can be either "sender" for a private chat with the user opening the link, "private", "group", "supergroup", or "channel". Returned only for Mini Apps launched from direct links. | 992 | chat_instance | String | _Optional._ Global identifier, uniquely corresponding to the chat from which the Mini App was opened. Returned only for Mini Apps launched from a direct link. | 993 | start_param | String | _Optional._ The value of the *startattach* parameter, passed [via link](#adding-bots-to-the-attachment-menu). Only returned for Mini Apps when launched from the attachment menu via link. \ 994 \ 995 The value of the `start_param` parameter will also be passed in the GET-parameter `tgWebAppStartParam`, so the Mini App can load the correct interface right away. | 996 | can_send_after | Integer | _Optional._ Time in seconds, after which a message can be sent via the [answerWebAppQuery](/bots/api/methods/answerwebappquery.md) method. | 997 | auth_date | Integer | Unix time when the form was opened. | 998 | hash | String | A hash of all passed parameters, which the bot server can use to [check their validity](#validating-data-received-via-the-mini-app). | 999 | signature | String | A signature of all passed parameters (except *hash*), which the third party can use to [check their validity](#validating-data-for-third-party-use). | 1000 === 1030,1090 === 1030 #### Validating data received via the Mini App 1031 1032 To validate data received via the Mini App, one should send the data from the *Telegram.WebApp.initData* field to the bot's backend. The data is a query string, which is composed of a series of field-value pairs. 1033 1034 You can verify the integrity of the data received by comparing the received *hash* parameter with the hexadecimal representation of the [HMAC-SHA-256](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hash-based_message_authentication_code) signature of the **data-check-string** with the secret key, which is the [HMAC-SHA-256](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hash-based_message_authentication_code) signature of the [bot's token](/bots/tutorial.md#obtain-your-bot-token) with the constant string `WebAppData` used as a key. 1035 1036 **Data-check-string** is a chain of all received fields, sorted alphabetically, in the format `key=` with a [line feed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newline) character (' 1037 ', 0x0A) used as separator – e.g., `'auth_date= 1038 query_id= 1039 user='`. 1040 1041 The full check might look like: 1042 1043 data_check_string = ... 1044 secret_key = HMAC_SHA256(, "WebAppData") 1045 if (hex(HMAC_SHA256(data_check_string, secret_key)) == hash) { 1046 // data is from Telegram 1047 } 1048 1049 To prevent the use of outdated data, you can additionally check the *auth_date* field, which contains a Unix timestamp of when it was received by the Mini App. 1050 1051 Once validated, the data may be used on your server. Complex data types are represented as JSON-serialized objects. 1052 1053 #### Validating data for Third-Party Use 1054 1055 If you need to share the data with a third party, they can validate the data without requiring access to your [bot's token](/bots/tutorial.md#obtain-your-bot-token). Simply provide them with the data from the *Telegram.WebApp.initData* field and your *bot_id*. 1056 1057 The integrity of the data can be verified by validating the received *signature* parameter, which is the base64url-encoded representation of the [Ed25519](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EdDSA) signature of the **data-check-string**. The verification is performed using the public key provided by Telegram. 1058 1059 **Data-check-string** is constructed as follows: 1060 1. Prepend the *bot_id*, followed by `:` and the constant string `WebAppData`. 1061 2. Add a [line feed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newline) character (`' 1062 '`, 0x0A). 1063 3. Append all received fields (except *hash* and *signature*), sorted alphabetically, in the format `key=`. 1064 4. Separate each key-value pair with a line feed character (`' 1065 '`, 0x0A). 1066 1067 **Example:** 1068 `'12345678:WebAppData 1069 auth_date= 1070 query_id= 1071 user='` 1072 1073 The verification process might look like this: 1074 1075 data_check_string = ... 1076 public_key = "" 1077 if (Ed25519_verify(public_key, data_check_string, signature)) { 1078 // data is valid and originated from Telegram 1079 } 1080 1081 > Telegram provides the following [Ed25519](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EdDSA) public keys for signature verification: 1082 > 1083 > **Test environment:** `40055058a4ee38156a06562e52eece92a771bcd8346a8c4615cb7376eddf72ec` (hex) 1084 > **Production:** `e7bf03a2fa4602af4580703d88dda5bb59f32ed8b02a56c187fe7d34caed242d` (hex) 1085 1086 To prevent the use of outdated data, the third party should additionally validate the *auth_date* field. This field contains a Unix timestamp indicating when the data was received by the Mini App. 1087 1088 Once validated, the data may be used. Complex data types are represented as JSON-serialized objects. 1089 1090 #### Events Available for Mini Apps

     4	
     5	> The Bot API is an HTTP-based interface created for developers keen on building bots for Telegram.
     6	To learn how to create and set up a bot, please consult our [**Introduction to Bots**](/bots.md) and [**Bot FAQ**](/bots/faq.md).

     8	### Recent changes

    10	Recent updates are listed in the [Bot API changelog](/bots/api-changelog.md).
    11	
    12	### Authorizing your bot
    13	
    14	Each bot is given a unique authentication token [when it is created](/bots/features.md#botfather). The token looks something like `123456:ABC-DEF1234ghIkl-zyx57W2v1u123ew11`, but we'll use simply **<token>** in this document instead. You can learn about obtaining tokens and generating new ones in [this document](/bots/features.md#botfather).
    15	
    16	### Making requests
    17	
    18	All queries to the Telegram Bot API must be served over HTTPS and need to be presented in this form: `https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME`. Like this for example:
    19	
    20		https://api.telegram.org/bot123456:ABC-DEF1234ghIkl-zyx57W2v1u123ew11/getMe
    21	
    22	We support **GET** and **POST** HTTP methods. We support four ways of passing parameters in Bot API requests:
    23	
    24	- [URL query string](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Query_string)
    25	- application/x-www-form-urlencoded
    26	- application/json (except for uploading files)
    27	- multipart/form-data (use to upload files)
    28	
    29	The response contains a JSON object, which always has a Boolean field 'ok' and may have an optional String field 'description' with a human-readable description of the result. If 'ok' equals *True*, the request was successful and the result of the query can be found in the 'result' field. In case of an unsuccessful request, 'ok' equals *False* and the error is explained in the 'description'. An Integer 'error_code' field is also returned, but its contents are subject to change in the future. Some errors may also have an optional field 'parameters' of the type [ResponseParameters](/bots/api/types/responseparameters.md), which can help to automatically handle the error.
    30	
    31	- All methods in the Bot API are case-insensitive.
    32	- All queries must be made using UTF-8.
    33	
    34	#### Making requests when getting updates
    35	
    36	If you're using [**webhooks**](/bots/api.md#getting-updates), you can perform a request to the Bot API while sending an answer to the webhook. Use either *application/json* or *application/x-www-form-urlencoded* or *multipart/form-data* response content type for passing parameters. Specify the method to be invoked in the *method* parameter of the request. It's not possible to know that such a request was successful or get its result.
    37	
    38	>Please see our [FAQ](/bots/faq.md#how-can-i-make-requests-in-response-to-updates) for examples.
    39	
    40	### Using a Local Bot API Server
    41	
    42	The Bot API server source code is available at [telegram-bot-api](https://github.com/tdlib/telegram-bot-api). You can run it locally and send the requests to your own server instead of `https://api.telegram.org`. If you switch to a local Bot API server, your bot will be able to:
    43	
    44	- Download files without a size limit.
    45	- Upload files up to 2000 MB.
    46	- Upload files using their local path and [the file URI scheme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File_URI_scheme).
    47	- Use an HTTP URL for the webhook.
    48	- Use any local IP address for the webhook.
    49	- Use any port for the webhook.
    50	- Set *max_webhook_connections* up to 100000.
    51	- Receive the absolute local path as a value of the *file_path* field without the need to download the file after a [getFile](/bots/api/methods/getfile.md) request.
    52	
    53	#### Do I need a Local Bot API Server
    54	
    55	The majority of bots will be OK with the default configuration, running on our servers. But if you feel that you need one of [these features](/bots/api.md#using-a-local-bot-api-server), you're welcome to switch to your own at any time.
    56	
    57	### Getting updates

    59	There are two mutually exclusive ways of receiving updates for your bot - the [getUpdates](/bots/api/methods/getupdates.md) method on one hand and [webhooks](/bots/api/methods/setwebhook.md) on the other. Incoming updates are stored on the server until the bot receives them either way, but they will not be kept longer than 24 hours.

Depending on the task, you can choose between lightweight regular messages and structured rich messages with headings, tables, media, documents, mathematical expressions and interactive controls. 859 860 Formatting is available on two levels: 861 862 - [**Rich Messages**](/bots/api/types/inputrichmessage.md) for advanced structured content 863 - [**Regular Messages**](/bots/api/methods/sendmessage.md) for lightweight formatted text. 864 865
866 868
869 870 > Send a message to [@RichTextDemoBot](https://t.me/richtextdemobot) to play around with an interactive **rich message** demo. 871 872 #### Rich Messages 873 874 Rich messages are designed for highly structured responses: reports, AI-streamed answers, documentation snippets, technical papers and similarly complex content. 875 876 These messages support both [**Rich Markdown**](/bots/api/rich-messages.md#rich-markdown-style) and [**Rich HTML**](/bots/api/rich-messages.md#rich-html-style). All they need to do is start a message with your bot's *@username* and enter a keyword. 184 185 Having received the query, your bot can return some results. As soon as the user selects one, it is sent to the **relevant chat**. This way, people can request and send content from your bot in any of their chats, groups or channels. 186 187 Remember that inline functionality has to be enabled via [@BotFather](https://t.me/botfather), or your bot will not receive inline [Updates](/bots/api/types/update.md). 188 189
190 191
192 193 > Examples of inline bots include [@gif](https://gif.t.me), [@bing](https://bing.t.me) and [@wiki](https://wiki.t.me). [Mini App](#mini-apps) bots can also be used inline – try typing [@durgerkingbot](https://durgerkingbot.t.me) in any chat. 194 195 #### Deep Linking 196 Telegram bots have a deep linking mechanism that allows **additional parameters** to be passed to the bot on startup. It could be a command that launches the bot – or an authentication token to connect the user's Telegram account to their account on another platform. 197 198 Each bot has a link that **opens a conversation** with it in Telegram – `https://t.me/`. Parameters can be added directly to this link to let your bot work with additional information on the fly, without any user input. 199 200 > A-Z, a-z, 0-9, _ and - are allowed. We recommend using base64url to encode parameters with binary and other types of content. The parameter can be up to 64 characters long. === features 420-470 === 420 ### Monetization 421 Telegram offers a **robust ecosystem** of monetization features, allowing any bot to support its development with **multiple revenue streams**. 422 423 #### Telegram Stars 424 Telegram Stars power all digital transactions between bots and users. Users can acquire Stars through in-app purchases via Apple and Google or via [@PremiumBot](https://t.me/premiumbot). 425 426 Bots can use the Stars they receive to [increase message limits](https://telegram.org/blog/dynamic-video-quality-and-more#increased-message-limits-for-bots), [send gifts](/bots/api/methods/sendgift.md) to users or [accept rewards](https://telegram.org/blog/monetization-for-channels) in Toncoin. 427 428
429 430
431 432 #### Digital Products 433 Services can use their bot to sell **digital goods** and **services** – like online courses, commissioned artwork and **items in games**. 434 435
436 439
440 441 #### Paid Media 442 Bots can post **paid photos** and **videos** – users can view the media only after paying to unlock it. This functionality is available where the bot can send messages in the target chat, including channel chats where it has the relevant paid-media permission and chats managed through a Business Connection. 443 444
445 448
449 450 #### Subscription Plans 451 Developers are able to **offer paid subscriptions** to their bot – adding **multiple tiers** of content and features tailored to their audience. 452 453
454
457
458 459 #### Revenue Sharing from Telegram Ads 460 Developers can participate in [revenue sharing](https://telegram.org/blog/monetization-for-channels) from [Telegram Ads](https://telegram.org/blog/monetization-for-channels#ton-based-ads) – receiving **50%** of the revenue from ads that appear in the chat with their bot. 461 462
463 466
467 468 ### Mini Apps 469 [Mini Apps](webapps) allow developers to create flexible interfaces that can be launched right inside Telegram – integrating seamlessly with the app and bringing complete services into the chat. 470 === features 1014-1034 === 1014 #### Local Bot API 1015 You can host and work with **your own instance** of our open-source [Bot API](/bots/api.md). 1016 The **source code** is available [here](https://github.com/tdlib/telegram-bot-api), along with a quick [installation guide](https://github.com/tdlib/telegram-bot-api#installation). 1017 1018 After **installing the server**, remember to use the [logOut](/bots/api/methods/logout.md) method before **redirecting requests** to your new local API URL. 1019 1020 > Your local instance accepts HTTP requests, so a TLS termination proxy has to be used to handle remote HTTPS requests. See the installation guide for the port and other server settings. 1021 1022 By hosting our API locally you'll gain access to **some upgrades**, including: 1023 1024 |API|Max File Download|Max File Upload|WHook URL|WHook Port|WHook Max Connections| 1025 |-----| 1026 |[Official](/bots/api.md#making-requests)|20MB|50MB|HTTPS|443,80,88,8443|1-100| 1027 |[Local](/bots/api.md#using-a-local-bot-api-server)|Unlimited|2000MB|HTTP|Any port|1-100000| 1028 1029 > You can find an exhaustive list [here](/bots/api.md#using-a-local-bot-api-server). 1030 All limits may be subject to change in the future, so make sure to follow [@BotNews](https://t.me/botnews). 1031 1032 ----- 1033 1034 ### BotFather

If you're looking for a general overview of Telegram Payments, check out the [Telegram blog](https://telegram.org/blog/payments-2-0-scheduled-voice-chats#payments-2-0). 11 12 If you are new to Telegram bots and would like to learn how to create and set up a bot, please consult our [**Introduction to Bots**](/bots.md) and [**Bot FAQ**](/bots/faq.md). 13 14 ### Overview 15 16 Payments are seamlessly integrated into Telegram, allowing you to sell digital goods and services in exchange for [Telegram Stars](https://telegram.org/blog/telegram-stars), an in-app virtual item that you can later convert to a reward. 17 18 With the Payments API, you’ll be able to: 19 20 - Send invoices to **any chat**, including to groups and channels. 21 - Create invoices that can be **forwarded** and used by **multiple buyers** to order things. 22 - Use [inline mode](/bots/inline.md) to help users show your goods and services to their friends and communities. 23 - Accept payments from users on mobile or **desktop apps**. 24 - Try [@DurgerKingBot](https://t.me/DurgerKingBot) to create a test invoice – or start a message with `@DurgerKingBot ...` in any chat for an **inline invoice**. 25 - Check out [Demo Shop](https://t.me/teststore) for an example of a [Telegram Channel](https://telegram.org/tour/channels) used as **virtual storefront**. 26 27
28 31
32 33 #### Star Pricing 34 Here is a table showing a breakdown of how much a user pays to acquire certain amounts of Stars, and the net proceeds received by the developer. Note that these amounts may vary from user to user due to VAT and other applicable fees that are outside of Telegram’s control. 35 36
37 38
39 40 #### How does this work? 41 42 You create a **bot** that offers **digital goods and services** to Telegram users. Merchant bots can send specially formatted **invoice messages** to users, groups or channels. If your bot supports [inline mode](/bots/inline.md), users can also send invoices to other chats *via the bot*, including to 1-on-1 chats with other users. 43 44 45 46 Invoice messages feature a **photo** and **description** of the product along with a prominent **Pay** button. Tapping this button opens a special payment interface in the Telegram app. 47 48 Since your bot sells **digital** goods and services, all transactions must be carried out in Telegram Stars, with currency tag `XTR`. Users can acquire Stars from Telegram using standard Apple and Google in-app purchases or via [@PremiumBot](https://t.me/premiumbot) and then use them to buy digital goods and services from you. 49 50 The invoice interface for digital goods and services is seamless and **doesn’t require** users to enter any personal information, like their full name, shipping address or credit card details. 51 52 > [Detailed information](#the-payments-api) and [step-by-step instructions](#step-by-step-process) are available below. 53 54 ---- 55 56 ### The Payments API 57 58 This section explores payments via Telegram's Bot API in more detail. 59 60 > This section is dedicated to the sale of **digital goods and services** – if you’re interested in selling **physical goods and services**, please check out our [dedicated page](/bots/payments.md). === stars 85-164 === 85 ### Step-by-Step Process 86 87 > See [Bot API: Payments](/bots/api.md#payments) for the complete list of available methods and objects. Be sure to provide the proper set of parameters to account for the type of goods you are selling, differentiating between digital and physical orders. 88 89 #### 1. Create Invoice 90 The user contacts `@merchantbot` and requests to purchase something. The bot forms an invoice message with a description of the goods or service and amount to be paid (expressed in Telegram Stars). There are two ways of creating an invoice: 91 92 ##### A. Bot Invoice 93 94 Use the [sendInvoice](/bots/api/methods/sendinvoice.md) method to generate an invoice and send it to a chat. You can pass an empty string as the *provider_token* parameter, since the invoice is for digital goods and services. 95 96 Invoice messages with a pay button can be sent to **chats of any type**: private chats with the user, groups, or channels. The resulting invoice message will look like this: 97 98
99 100

Bot Invoice

101 102 > Remember to specify `XTR` in the `currency` field, since all sales of **digital goods and services** are carried out exclusively in Telegram Stars. 103 104 ##### B. Inline Invoice 105 106 If `@merchantbot` supports [inline mode](/bots/inline.md), you can use [inputInvoiceMessageContent](/bots/api/types/inputinvoicemessagecontent.md) to allow users to share invoices for your goods and services to their one-on-one chats with friends, or to their groups and channels. These invoices will have a **Pay button** that can be used multiple times. 107 108
109 110

Inline Invoice

111 112 #### 2. Choose Forwarding Behavior 113 114 There are two ways for handling **forwarded copies** of your invoices, controlled by the parameter *start_parameter* in the [sendInvoice](/bots/api/methods/sendinvoice.md) method. 115 116 * **A. Multi-chat invoice.** Forwarded copies show a **Pay button**, which multiple users can press and attempt to pay for the goods or services. [Inline invoices](#b-inline-invoice) are always multi-chat invoices. 117 * **B. Single-chat invoice.** Invoice can only be paid from the chat to which it was sent, *forwarded copies* show a **URL button** with a deep link to the bot. The deep link can be used to generate a similar invoice in the chat with the bot, to show an error message, or for other purposes. [More info on Deep Linking »](/bots.md#deep-linking) 118 119 If a *single-chat invoice* is sent to the chat with `@merchantbot`, it can only be paid **once**. If a *single-chat invoice* is sent to any other chat, it can be paid **many times** by many users. 120 121 > To get a better understanding of how this works, try toggling the *"Pay from Forwards"* parameter when creating invoices with our demo [@ShopBot](https://t.me/shopbot). 122 123 Regardless of whether or not the **Pay** button is available in an invoice, the merchant bot always has the power to decide whether or not to accept new payments for a particular invoice. 124 125 #### 3. Pre-Checkout 126 The user purchases Stars from Telegram (if necessary), then presses the pay button. At this moment the Bot API sends an [Update](/bots/api/types/update.md) with the field *pre_checkout_query* that contains all the available information about the order to the bot. 127 128 Your bot must reply using [answerPrecheckoutQuery](/bots/api/methods/answerprecheckoutquery.md) within **10 seconds** after receiving this update or the transaction is canceled. 129 130 The bot may return an error if it can't process the order for any reason. We highly recommend specifying a reason for failure to complete the order in human readable form (e.g. *"Sorry, we're all out of rubber duck digital posters! Would you be interested in a cast iron bear digital poster instead?"*). Telegram will display this reason to the user. 131 132 > **Warning:** It is critical to make sure your bot **only** accepts multiple payments when the order can be processed correctly. This is especially important if you are using [multi-chat](#2-choose-forwarding-behavior), [inline](#2-choose-forwarding-behavior) or [single-chat, multi-use](#2-choose-forwarding-behavior) invoices. 133 134 #### 4. Checkout 135 If the bot confirms the order and the payment is successful, the API will send a receipt message of the type [*successful_payment*](/bots/api/types/message.md) from the user. Once your bot receives this message, it should proceed with sending the digital goods or services purchased by the user. 136 137 > **Warning:** You **must** always check that you received a [*successful_payment*](/bots/api/types/message.md) update before delivering the goods or services purchased by the user – simply answering a *pre_checkout_query* does not guarantee a successful order or payment. 138 139 If the invoice message was sent in the chat with `@merchantbot`, it becomes a Receipt in the UI for the user – they can open this receipt at any time and see all the details of the transaction: 140 141
142 143

Receipt

144 145 If the message was sent to any other chat, the **Pay button** remains and can be used again. It is up to the merchant bot whether to actually accept multiple payments. 146 147 ### Going Live 148 149 Once you've tested everything and confirmed that your payments implementation works, you're ready to go live – to do so, simply switch to the production environment. 150 151 Before your merchant bot goes into live mode, please ensure the following: 152 153 #### Live Checklist 154 155 - We highly recommend turning on [2-step verification](https://telegram.org/faq#q-how-does-2-step-verification-work) for the Telegram account that controls your bot. 156 - You as the bot owner have **full responsibility** in case any conflicts or disputes arise. You must be prepared to correctly process disputes and chargebacks. 157 - To prevent any misunderstandings and possible legal issues, make sure your bot can respond to a /terms command (or offers a similarly easy way of accessing your Terms and Conditions). Your Terms and Conditions should be written in a clear way and easy to understand for your users. The users must confirm that they have read and agree to your terms before they make the purchase. 158 - Your bot must provide support for its customers, either by responding to a /support command or by some other clearly communicated means. Users must have a clear way of contacting you about their purchases and you must process their support requests in a timely fashion. You must notify your users that Telegram support or [bot support](https://t.me/botsupport) will not be able to help them with purchases made via your bot. 159 - Verify your server hardware and software are stable. Use backups to make sure that you don't lose data about your users' payments. 160 - Make sure that you have read, understood and agreed to the Telegram [Terms of Service](https://telegram.org/tos) and, by extension, to the Telegram [Bot Platform Developer Terms of Service](https://telegram.org/tos/bot-developers). 161 162 ------- 163 164 ### FAQ === stars 190-205 === 190 #### Q: How can I issue refunds? 191 192 Refunds for **digital goods and services** can be issued via the [refundStarPayment](/bots/api/methods/refundstarpayment.md) method on the Telegram Bot API. 193 194 #### Q: What can I do with Telegram Stars? 195 196 Stars can be used to [place Telegram Ads](https://telegram.org/tos/bot-developers#6-2-3-advertising-with-stars) for your TPA or to [accept a reward](https://telegram.org/tos/bot-developers#6-2-4-rewards-for-stars) for the monetary value that Telegram assigns to each Star. 197 198 > For more details on what terms regulate your engagement with Telegram Stars, please reference [Section 6.2. Digital Goods and Services](https://telegram.org/tos/bot-developers#6-2-digital-goods-and-services) of the Telegram Bot Platform Developer Terms of Service. 199 200 203 204 #### Q: How do I support payments in my third-party app that uses the Telegram API? 205
